Al Jazeera (Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and Reuters) — "Public workers in France strike over pay as student protests turn violent". Published 30 September 2026.
*** DATE CAUTION: the strike and marches described took place on TUESDAY 29 SEPTEMBER 2026. The article's own text says "police on Tuesday estimated a turnout of 30,000 in the capital". This is a 29 Sep event with a 30 Sep write-up, NOT a 30 Sep development. ***
Retrieved via WebFetch. Figures and quotes as returned by the tool.

PARTICIPATION
- Union (CGT) estimate: 300,000 nationwide
- Police estimate for Paris: 30,000
- Teachers/school staff on strike: just over 11%
- Other civil servants: fewer than 1 in 10
- Schools with protests: 400+; schools blockaded: 40; attempted blockades: 44

ARRESTS & INJURIES
- Detained: 440 people (roughly two-thirds led to police custody)
- Students/staff wounded: 10
- Law enforcement injured: 48

MONEY
- Government proposes 2 billion euros of savings via a public-sector salary freeze for 2027
- Union demand: 6% raise
- (Al Jazeera also gives the euro figure as "$2.3bn")

DIRECT QUOTES (verbatim as returned)
Sophie Binet, General Secretary of the General Confederation of Labour (CGT): "This anger is not going away. The government must look again at the budget."
  — Al Jazeera also reports Binet called the protests "a red alert" and gave the government 48 hours to reverse the planned cuts before her union decides on further strike action.
Laurent Nunez, Interior Minister, to BFMTV: "Violence is never legitimate. There is nothing that justifies violence."
Edouard Geffray, Education Minister, in a social media statement: "This violence is unspeakable."
Mael Breton, final-year student at Helene-Boucher school: "We want fewer police because we think there is a huge amount of police repression."

FORWARD HOOK (the only genuine 30 Sep / 1 Oct angle): the government unveils its draft 2027 budget on Thursday 1 October; the presidential election is seven months away.
